topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Mutations and susceptibility in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce evolving cancer clones and why cells differ in their susceptibility to that process.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than attributing cancer solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, with their activity depending on how the body processes an exposure.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a tumour-promoting environment for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the circumstances of the exposed tissue condition carcinogenic effects and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogen specificity.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence can establish carcinogenic effects while showing why no available method fully captures cancer causation.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them in everyday risk–benefit decisions.
